Figure 2: CARGO-VL overview. A real CMC-Bench ChartQA input illustrates how the same question is instantiated as an aligned (A), image-correct (V), text-correct (T), or both-wrong (N) evidence bundle. CARGO-VL jointly scores all four conditions with pointwise and transition rewards, weakest-condition protection, and risk constraints, then optimizes the policy with an SFT warm start followed by constrained GRPO. The protocol panel records the training configuration; it reports no performance values. The XMC training set extends the four-condition recipe to fresh TextVQA and ScienceQA examples used only for training.

Table 3: Main leaderboard: CMC-Bench holdout / Modality-Bias (mean over seeds {42, 43, 44}). Left block matches the official CMC-Bench Table 3 suite (Catapang 2026): Acc(c) from judge labels; MPBimg = Nimg/(Nimg +Ntxt) and MPBtxt = 1− MPBimg among single-modality commits (values >50 indicate a systematic lean); MFR on conflict conditions; ConfabR/CDR = NEITHER/ABSTAIN on conflict trials; diagnostic HR = ConfabR+CDR (no preferred direction: ConfabR↓while CDR↑); ∆Acc = Acc(aligned) −meanAcc(conflict). Right block matches Mixed Signals bias reporting (Pezeshkpour, Aminnaseri, and Hruschka 2025): B = (%Img − %Txt). Higher is better except ConfabR and ∆Acc; for B and MPB, closer to zero / 50–50 is better; HR is not ranked. Best values are marked in bold with underline. Ablations reuse these columns in Table 4 and Figure 4.
